userStories.title: Soft-deleting a project stops its VCS polling and keeps its budget pauses
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Consume the project deletion event to deactivate VCS polling and retain soft-deleted projects' budget scopes.

**Motivation** — `PrismaBudgetRepository.scopeExists` treats the deleted project as gone, so `BudgetSweeper` deletes its policies within 60 s and a paused budget stops holding.

**Approach** — **US-002.** `VcsProjectDeletionListener` (`@SystemWriter('system.project.quiesce')`) runs
`repo.deactivateConnectionsForProject(projectId): Promise<string[]>` (set `isActive: false` on the project's active
connections, answer their ids) inside `runAsSystemWriter` + `txManager.run`, records one `system.project.quiesce`
entry with `resourceType: 'vcs-connection'` per deactivated connection, then calls `unschedulePolling` for each id
after the commit. Errors are logged, never rethrown.

`PrismaBudgetRepository.scopeExists`. Baseline: `case 'project'` counts `{ id, deletedAt: null }`. Target: counts
`{ id }`.

`PrismaVcsRepository.findVcsConnectionById` and `findPollingConnections`. Baseline: no project filter. Target:
`project: { deletedAt: null }` in `where` (`findVcsConnectionById` becomes a `findFirst`).

**Scope** — In: VCS listener/provider registration, deactivation repository contract/query, polling-read deletion filters, project scope existence and retention tests. Add the VcsProjectDeletionListener writer-map and permission inventory row using the existing system.project.quiesce key. Update the D166 budget-repository expectation to true. Out: US-001's event/cancellation implementation, US-003's issue uniqueness/in-flight guard, and US-004's placement changes. The VCS webhook intake of a deleted project is not changed; findVcsConnectionByProjectSlug already filters deletedAt. No hard-delete/restore path is added and deleted-project policies remain until a hard delete; ordinary budget rollover behavior remains unchanged.

**Interface** — `repo.deactivateConnectionsForProject(projectId): Promise<string[]>`; `VcsPollingService.unschedulePolling(connectionId)` removes the interval and the scheduled id. Consume `PROJECT_SOFT_DELETED` and `ProjectSoftDeletedEvent` produced by US-001; `onProjectSoftDeleted(event: ProjectSoftDeletedEvent): Promise<void>` never rejects. AuditRecorder.record runs within the listener's system-writer transaction. If that transaction fails, log error and do not unschedule from the listener; the next polling tick's deletion-filtered lookup returns null and causes unscheduling. The integration seam must trigger real ProjectsService.softDeleteById and await its real EventEmitter2 listeners, not manually imitate event delivery.

userStories.title: A VCS issue imports into at most one ticket per project
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce import uniqueness in PostgreSQL and prevent overlapping polling ticks for one connection.

**Motivation** — A "Sync now" during a polling tick, two webhook deliveries, or an overlapping tick each import the same issue twice.

**Approach** — **US-003.** The migration clears `externalVcsId` on every duplicate except the lowest ticket `number` per
`(projectId, externalVcsId)`, then creates the unique index:

```sql
UPDATE "Ticket" t SET "externalVcsId" = NULL
WHERE t."externalVcsId" IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM "Ticket" o WHERE o."projectId" = t."projectId" AND o."externalVcsId" = t."externalVcsId" AND o."number" < t."number");
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "Ticket_projectId_externalVcsId_key" ON "Ticket"("projectId", "externalVcsId");
```

`syncIssue` keeps its existing pre-check and maps a null `createTicketFromIssue` result to
`{ action: 'skipped', reason: 'Ticket with this external VCS ID already exists' }`. Outside a transaction,
`runWithTicketNumberRetry` has already rolled the attempt back when the violation reaches the repository's catch, so
answering null is safe; inside an enclosing transaction (the approval-executed manual sync) the violation propagates
and that transaction fails as a whole. `VcsPollingService` keeps `private readonly inFlight = new Set<string>()`;
`pollConnection` returns at once when the id is in the set, adds it before the poll and deletes it in `finally`.

`PrismaVcsRepository.createTicketFromIssue`. Baseline: answers `CreateTicketFromIssueResult` or throws. Target:
answers `CreateTicketFromIssueResult | null`; null when the insert hit `isUniqueViolation(error, 'externalVcsId')`
and `this.txManager.isInTransaction()` was false when the call started; any other error, and that violation inside an
enclosing transaction, is rethrown.

**Scope** — In: Ticket @@unique([projectId, externalVcsId]) and the specified cleanup/index migration, nullable repository interface/consumer, and pollConnection in-flight lifecycle. Keep @@index([externalVcsId]), pre-check semantics including deleted imports, and the ticket-number retry helper's behavior. Out: US-002 deletion filtering/deactivation, placement and other schema soft deletes. The approval-executed manual sync (prepareSyncAll, isolate:false) is not made to skip an aborted transaction. The webhook issues.opened path and manual sync routes get no in-flight guard of their own.

**Interface** — `createTicketFromIssue(project: { id: string }, issue: VcsIssue, externalVcsId: string, onCreated?: OnTicketCreated): Promise<CreateTicketFromIssueResult | null>`; update IVcsRepository consistently. `isUniqueViolation(error, field)` matches P2002 via the constraint target helper; never inspect error.meta directly. `Ticket_projectId_externalVcsId_key` contains externalVcsId but not number, so isTicketNumberConflict does not match it and runWithTicketNumberRetry rethrows it. Capture ambient transaction state before invoking the retry helper; catch outside its rolled-back attempt. Existing audit onCreated remains inside the ticket insert transaction. Tests must exercise two concurrent syncIssue callers and the enclosing-transaction failure path with a real database, plus independent connection polling and finally cleanup after failure.

userStories.title: Runner fills scan only jobs the runner can take and page past the first 50
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Filter runner-specific QUEUED candidates in SQL and scan bounded cursor pages in both fill paths.

**Motivation** — 50 jobs that this runner can never take (pinned elsewhere, the other kind, a deleted project) hide every newer job, and nothing moves them out of the window.

**Approach** — **US-004: scan composition.** The order is: SQL filter, then the page loop, then the existing per-job checks.

1. `findQueuedPage` filters in SQL: `state: QUEUED`, `project: { deletedAt: null }`, `command` equal to `'THREAD'`
   when `threads` is true and not equal to `'THREAD'` otherwise, and `OR: [{ pinnedRunnerId: null }, { pinnedRunnerId: runnerId }]`.
   It orders by `[{ queuedAt: 'asc' }, { id: 'asc' }]`, takes `limit`, and with `after` adds
   `OR: [{ queuedAt: { gt: after.queuedAt } }, { queuedAt: after.queuedAt, id: { gt: after.id } }]` (both `OR`s go
   under one `AND`).
2. `fillRunner` and `fillRunnerThreads` read pages of `QUEUED_SCAN_LIMIT` (50) rows, starting with `after: null` and
   continuing from the last row of each page, until the free slots reach 0, a page holds fewer than
   `QUEUED_SCAN_LIMIT` rows, or `MAX_QUEUED_SCAN_PAGES` (10, exported from `placement-rules.ts`) pages were read. When
   the page cap ends the scan while slots are still free and the last page was full, the service logs a `warn` naming
   the runner (`.nax/rules/api-data.md` pagination rule).
3. Each scanned id goes through the unchanged loop body: `lockById` with `skipLocked`, the state and kind checks, the
   budget-pause cancel, the misfit check, `assign`.

**Scope** — In: replace findQueuedIds in the domain contract/Prisma implementation, export cursor/filter types and page cap, page both fill loops, update their repository doubles, preserve budgets/CAS/lock/load/live behavior. Out: US-001 project cancellation, US-002 VCS/budgets and all other fixes. Permanent misfits remain QUEUED; labels/profile matching stay per-job; dashboard findQueuedWindow(QUEUED_SCAN_LIMIT) is not paged; placeJob is unchanged; no new FleetJob index is added.

**Interface** — `findQueuedPage(filter: QueuedScanFilter, limit: number, after: QueuedCursor | null): Promise<QueuedCursor[]>` where `QueuedScanFilter = { runnerId: string; threads: boolean }` and `QueuedCursor = { id: string; queuedAt: Date }`. Export both from fleet/jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts, remove findQueuedIds, and export MAX_QUEUED_SCAN_PAGES=10 from placement-rules.ts. Keep QUEUED_SCAN_LIMIT=50. Preserve per-pass addJobToLoad accounting and post-commit publishing/notifying. Existing trust-domain, project-code, project-thread and koda-tools specs supply { id, queuedAt } rows instead of ids; the project-thread expectation must assert { runnerId, threads: true }. Test actual SQL pagination including equal timestamps and both real fill entry points; later jobs after a capped scan wait for a subsequent sync.

userStories.title: Ticket assignments create owner links in the entity graph
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make the entity graph consume the assignment payload actually emitted by TicketsService.assign.

**Motivation** — `TicketsService.assign` records `{ assignedTo, assigneeType }`, but `EntityGraphService.onTicketEvent` reads `assignedToUserId` and `assignedToAgentId`, so no real assignment ever creates a `TICKET_TO_OWNER` link.

**Approach** — The entity graph's `assigned` handler reads `assignedTo` and `assigneeType`, the keys `TicketsService.assign` sends, and a DB-backed contract test drives the producer into the consumer.

`InMemoryEntityStore` (`apps/api/src/entity-graph/in-memory-entity-store.ts`) exposes `findLinksBySource`.
`EntityGraphOutboxSubscriber` registers `ticket_event` on `FanOutPublisher` and maps the payload to
`EntityGraphService.onTicketEvent`.

For assigneeType 'user', upsert owner:<assignedTo> with metadata { userId: assignedTo }; for 'agent', use { agentId: assignedTo }. Upsert the ticket node as before even when assignedTo is null; create no owner link for null assignment or a missing/unsupported discriminant. Correct existing unit fixtures using invented assignedToUserId/assignedToAgentId event keys to the producer's real shape without changing their expected graph links. The contract tests must run TicketsService.assign against the DB, take its actual stored ticket_event outbox payload, and hand that payload to the handler the real EntityGraphOutboxSubscriber registers on FanOutPublisher, backed by InMemoryEntityStore.

**Scope** — In: assigned-event consumer, corrected fixtures and producer-to-consumer DB contract for user and agent assignments. Out: other stories' quiesce/import/soft-delete work, rebuild/backfill changes, and assignment removal cleanup. Assignment removal (assignedTo:null) does not delete an existing TICKET_TO_OWNER link.

**Interface** — Preserve `EntityGraphService.onTicketEvent(event: TicketEvent): Promise<void>` and the subscriber's ticket_event mapping. The assignment data contract is `{ assignedTo: 'u1', assigneeType: 'user' }`, `{ assignedTo: 'a1', assigneeType: 'agent' }` or `{ assignedTo: null, assigneeType: null }`. No new public endpoint or payload schema is added.

userStories.title: FTS optimize runs under the table's write lock
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Pass lock-aware optimize tasks to all FTS strategies without deadlocking held KB write sessions.

**Motivation** — `LanceTableManager.exclusive` serialises writes per table, and `VectorStoreService.optimizeTable` honours it, but the counter, cron and first-access optimize paths call `table.optimize()` directly and can race a knowledge `replaceFile`.

**Approach** — **US-006.** `VectorStoreService` builds the task for its table and passes it instead of the raw table:

```ts
const optimize: OptimizeTask = () => this.lanceTable.exclusive(`project_${projectId}`, async () => { await table.optimize(); });
```

`CounterOptimizeStrategy.onInsert` at the threshold starts `optimizeInBackground(optimize, projectId, this.logger)`
and resolves without waiting for it, because `onInsert` can run inside a held write session of the same table, and
awaiting `exclusive` there deadlocks; the queued optimize runs once the session releases. `CronOptimizeStrategy` keeps a
`Map<string, OptimizeTask>` and awaits each task on its tick (never inside a held session).
`ManualOptimizeStrategy.onFirstAccess` passes the task to `optimizeInBackground`. The first-access hook passes the
same kind of task.

`LanceTableManager.exclusive(tableName, fn)` is a non-reentrant promise-chain mutex: awaiting it from inside a
section that already holds the same table deadlocks.

**Scope** — In: OptimizeTask interface, counter/cron/manual signatures and call sites, optimizeInBackground task/error handling, VectorStore first-access and insertion closures, all existing strategy/vector-store expectations and held-session integration. Out: the other eleven stories; VectorStoreService.optimizeTable already runs under exclusive and is unchanged.

**Interface** — `type OptimizeTask = () => Promise<void>` exported from fts-optimize-strategy.interface.ts. `onInsert(projectId: string, optimize: OptimizeTask): Promise<void>` and `onFirstAccess(projectId: string, optimize: OptimizeTask): void`; `optimizeInBackground(optimize, projectId, logger)` takes the task. Keep onDestroy/clearProject semantics. Background execution catches both synchronous throws and promise rejections and logs warn as today. Cron clears/executes dirty tasks once per tick unless new inserts occur.

userStories.title: Deleting an agent is a soft delete that frees its slug
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Tombstone deleted agents without severing historical foreign keys, while freeing their original slug and disabling their key.

**Motivation** — The optional relations default to `SET NULL`, so the agent's comments become authorless and its tickets lose `createdByAgentId` and `assignedToAgentId`.

**Approach** — **US-007.** `PrismaAgentRepository.softDeleteById(id): Promise<AgentWithCapabilities | null>` runs, inside the
caller's transaction, `updateMany({ where: { id, deletedAt: null }, data: { deletedAt: now, status: 'OFFLINE', slug: slug + '~deleted-' + id, apiKeyHash: 'deleted:' + randomBytes(32).toString('hex') } })`
(the slug read first with `findFirst({ where: { id, deletedAt: null } })`), answers null when no row was found or
updated, and otherwise re-reads the row with `findUnique({ where: { id }, include: { capabilities: true } })`
(`updateManyAndReturn` cannot `include`). Renaming the slug frees it, so a new agent may take the old slug.
`AgentsService.remove(slug)` and `removeById(id)` call it instead of the hard deletes, throw
`NotFoundAppException({}, 'agents')` on null, keep removing the bindings in the same transaction, keep the
`agent.delete` audit entry, and answer the agent as it was before the delete: `softDeleteById` returns the re-read row
with `slug` replaced by the slug it pre-read, so the response DTO and the audit summary `deleted <slug>` carry the
original slug. `deleteBySlug` and `deleteById` are removed.

**Scope** — In: Agent.deletedAt DateTime? and @@index([deletedAt]), migration, conditional identity-based soft delete with capabilities/original-slug response, service deletion/bindings/audit/cache behavior and related regression expectations. Out: US-008's finder/auth/principalExists filters and rotation/capability guards; comments/project changes belong to other stories. Other modules that join Agent for display (audit, tickets, assignees, notifications, reviews, schedules) keep reading the row, so a deleted agent's name still shows on its past work. Do not edit the read-only .nax/rules/api-data.md.

**Interface** — `PrismaAgentRepository.softDeleteById(id): Promise<AgentWithCapabilities | null>` replaces deleteBySlug/deleteById. `AgentsService.remove(slug): Promise<AgentResponseDto>` and `removeById(id): Promise<AgentResponseDto>` preserve their public response's original slug; a null write result becomes NotFoundAppException({}, 'agents') including concurrent deletes. Keep immutable id targeting for approval execution, removal of all bindings and the single agent.delete audit entry in the same transaction, and auth invalidation after commit. Tombstoned slug storage is exactly `${slug}~deleted-${id}`; dead-key storage is 'deleted:' plus 32 random bytes as hex. **Goal** — Exclude tombstoned agents from live identity lookups, authentication and new binding/key/capability writes.

**Motivation** — Before US-007, `DELETE /agents/:slug` is a hard delete; the new tombstone must keep history without leaving a usable principal.

**Approach** — **US-008.** Every finder in `PrismaAgentRepository` (`findAll`, `findBySlug`, `findById`,
